```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction1"))$reference`
* Description (fraction 1): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction1"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-33160-0> (open access)

Morschhauser et al. (2018) built a five-compartment pharmacokinetic model of
ibritumomab tiuxetan, the anti-CD20 murine antibody that carries
90Y in radioimmunotherapy (RIT). They used the 111In-labelled imaging
surrogate, which was given before each of the two RIT fractions of the FIZZ
trial, and quantified it by whole-body SPECT/CT at 4, 24, 96 and 168 h. The
blood volume inside each organ was subtracted from the organ signal (their
Figure 1), so the organ compartments hold extravascular (tissue) antibody.
The authors used the Kinetica 5.0 Designer module to fit 30 candidate
structures to each patient and kept the one with the best AIC (their
Figure 3):

* blood is the central compartment, which receives the infusion and is the
  only site of elimination;
* blood exchanges in both directions with the L2-L4 lumbar vertebrae
  (`k12` / `k21`), the liver (`k13` / `k31`) and a deep compartment holding
  the remaining organs and the tumor (`k15` / `k51`);
* the spleen takes up antibody from blood (`k14`) and drains to the liver
  (`k43`), not back to blood.

The first fraction (F1) and the second fraction (F2) were fitted separately
and were not pooled. Table 3 reports the mean (SD) of the per-patient
estimates for each fraction, and nlmixr2lib packages each fraction as its
own model:

* `Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction1` -- F1, 19 patients;
* `Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction2` -- F2, 13 patients.

**Read this before using either model.** The paper never prints the deep
compartment's constants `k15` and `k51`, and the constants it does print
are not consistent with its own blood summary statistics (see
[Internal consistency of the published parameters](#internal-consistency-of-the-published-parameters)).
The packaged models implement Figure 3 as printed, as a mass-conserving
amount model, with `k15 = k51 = 0`. They therefore reproduce the published
structure and rate constants, but **not** the published blood
concentration-time course, MRT or half-life. The deviations are quantified
below.

# Population

The dosimetric subset of the FIZZ phase II trial (NCT01493479) treated
adults at Lille university hospital who had previously untreated,
CD20-positive follicular lymphoma needing treatment (paper Table 1). Imaging
after F1 was available for 19 patients (5 men and 14 women; mean age 58.8
years, range 28-80; mean weight 71.2 kg, range 49-100; FLIPI low /
intermediate / high risk 6 / 4 / 9). Imaging after F2 was available for 13
of them (3 men and 10 women; mean age 59.6 years; mean weight 72.9 kg,
range 49-83). F2 was cancelled for six patients because of haematologic
toxicity after F1 or because they developed human anti-mouse antibodies.
Mean tumor volume fell from 6751 mm3 before F1 to 1850 mm3 before F2.

Each fraction was preceded by two rituximab infusions (250 mg/m2) given 7-8
days apart, to saturate circulating CD20 binding sites. The 111In-ibritumomab
tiuxetan imaging dose (138 MBq at a specific activity of 138 MBq/mg, i.e.
1 mg of antibody) was given intravenously with the first rituximab infusion.
The therapeutic 90Y-ibritumomab tiuxetan dose was 11.1 MBq/kg per fraction
(maximum 888 MBq), with the fractions 8-12 weeks apart.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
readModelDb("Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction1")()$population$n_subjects
readModelDb("Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction2")()$population$n_subjects
```

# Source trace

Every value comes from paper Table 3. The paper reports clearance in mL/min
and the rate constants in min^-1; the model files multiply each by 60 so
that the models run in hours. The paper numbers the compartments 1 blood,
2 L2-L4 vertebrae, 3 liver, 4 spleen and 5 deep, and nlmixr2lib uses
role-based names for the same states.

| Model parameter / equation | Paper symbol | F1 (Table 3) | F2 (Table 3) | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | Blood clearance | 1.03 mL/min | 0.74 mL/min | Table 3, Blood, 'Clearance' |
| `lvc` | Blood Vd | 4131.0 mL | 4064.8 mL | Table 3, Blood, 'Vd' |
| `lkin_bonemarrow` | k12 | 1.11E-4 min^-1 | 0.60E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Vertebrae L2-L4 |
| `lkout_bonemarrow` | k21 | 1.05E-4 min^-1 | 0.96E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Vertebrae L2-L4 |
| `lkin_liver` | k13 | 1.80E-4 min^-1 | 2.05E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Liver |
| `lkout_liver` | k31 | 2.32E-4 min^-1 | 1.77E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Liver |
| `lkin_spleen` | k14 (row printed 'k13') | 2.11E-4 min^-1 | 1.17E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Spleen; Figure 3 |
| `lk_spleen_liver` | k43 (row printed 'k31') | 1.26E-4 min^-1 | 1.64E-4 min^-1 | Table 3, Spleen; Figure 3 |
| `kin_other` | k15 | not printed, fixed 0 | not printed, fixed 0 | Figure 3 only |
| `kout_other` | k51 | not printed, fixed 0 | not printed, fixed 0 | Figure 3 only |
| `kel <- cl / vc` | kel | derived | derived | Methods: kel is first-order elimination from blood |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(bonemarrow)`, `d/dt(liver)`, `d/dt(spleen)`, `d/dt(other)` | -- | -- | -- | Figure 3; Results, 'Pharmacokinetic model' |
| `Cc <- central / vc` | blood concentration | -- | -- | Table 3 Vd; Figure 2 (blood) |

# Simulation

Both models are typical-value models with no between-subject or residual
variability, so one deterministic solve per fraction is enough. The 1 mg
(1000 ug) imaging dose is given as an intravenous bolus into blood. The
paper does not state an infusion duration, and a few minutes of infusion
would not change anything on the hours-to-weeks time scale of the data.

```{r simulate}
dose_ug <- 1000

models <- c(
  F1 = "Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction1",
  F2 = "Morschhauser_2018_ibritumomabTiuxetan_fraction2"
)

# A long grid is needed: with k15 = k51 = 0 the terminal half-life is ~2 weeks.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(24, 4000, by = 2))))

simulate_fraction <- function(fraction, id) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ug, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id, fraction = fraction)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(models[[fraction]]), events = ev, keep = "fraction")
  as.data.frame(sim) |> dplyr::mutate(id = id)
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  simulate_fraction("F1", 1L),
  simulate_fraction("F2", 2L)
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2 -- blood concentration

The observed means below were read from Figure 2 of Morschhauser 2018 by
the maintainers, to about +/- 0.005 ug/mL. They are given only for
comparison and are not used by the model.

```{r observed-fig2}
fig2_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fraction, ~time, ~blood, ~bonemarrow, ~liver, ~spleen,
  "F1",       4,    0.300,  0.003,       0.010,  0.008,
  "F1",      24,    0.215,  0.031,       0.063,  0.067,
  "F1",      96,    0.090,  0.059,       0.121,  0.109,
  "F1",     168,    0.050,  0.053,       0.114,  0.097,
  "F2",       4,    0.310,  0.001,       0.010,  0.006,
  "F2",      24,    0.235,  0.016,       0.064,  0.044,
  "F2",      96,    0.110,  0.041,       0.134,  0.072,
  "F2",     168,    0.060,  0.042,       0.139,  0.067
)
```

```{r figure-2-blood, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 200) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = fraction)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = fig2_obs, aes(time, blood, colour = fraction),
    shape = 17, size = 2.5
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Blood 111In-ibritumomab tiuxetan (ug/mL)",
    colour = "Fraction",
    title = "Blood concentration: packaged model (lines) vs. Figure 2 means (points)",
    caption = "Replicates the blood panel of Figure 2 of Morschhauser 2018."
  )
```

```{r figure-2-blood-table}
blood_cmp <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% fig2_obs$time) |>
  dplyr::select(fraction, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2_obs |> dplyr::select(fraction, time, blood), by = c("fraction", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = Cc / blood)
stopifnot(nrow(blood_cmp) == 8L)

blood_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Fraction" = fraction,
    "Time (h)" = time,
    "Model Cc (ug/mL)" = Cc,
    "Figure 2 mean (ug/mL)" = blood,
    "Model / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Blood concentration, model vs. Figure 2.")
```

The modelled blood concentration falls too fast. By 96 h it is about a
quarter of the observed mean (F1) or about a third (F2). The reasons are
discussed under
[Internal consistency of the published parameters](#internal-consistency-of-the-published-parameters).

## Figure 2 -- organ tissue concentrations

The model states hold organ tissue amounts (ug). Figure 2 plots tissue
concentrations, but the paper does not print the tissue volumes it used. As
an approximation, the maintainers derived organ masses from paper Table 2 as
blood volume in the organ divided by blood volume per gram of organ (L2-L4
vertebrae 8.15 / 0.15 = 54 g, liver 485 / 0.29 = 1672 g, spleen
81.5 / 0.28 = 291 g), and assumed a density of 1 g/mL. Table 2 pools the two
fractions, so the same masses are used for both.

```{r figure-2-organs, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
organ_mass_g <- c(bonemarrow = 8.15 / 0.15, liver = 485 / 0.29, spleen = 81.5 / 0.28)

organ_sim <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 200) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    fraction, time,
    bonemarrow = bonemarrow / organ_mass_g[["bonemarrow"]],
    liver = liver / organ_mass_g[["liver"]],
    spleen = spleen / organ_mass_g[["spleen"]]
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(bonemarrow, liver, spleen), names_to = "organ", values_to = "conc")

organ_obs <- fig2_obs |>
  dplyr::select(-blood) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(bonemarrow, liver, spleen), names_to = "organ", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(organ_sim, aes(time, conc, colour = fraction)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = organ_obs, shape = 17, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~organ, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Tissue concentration (ug/mL)",
    colour = "Fraction",
    title = "Organ tissue: packaged model (lines) vs. Figure 2 means (points)",
    caption = "Replicates the organ panels of Figure 2 of Morschhauser 2018 (organ masses derived from Table 2)."
  )
```

```{r figure-2-organ-table}
organ_cmp <- organ_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(96, 168)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(organ_obs, by = c("fraction", "time", "organ"), suffix = c("_model", "_obs")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = conc_model / conc_obs)
stopifnot(nrow(organ_cmp) == 12L)

organ_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Fraction" = fraction,
    "Time (h)" = time,
    "Organ" = organ,
    "Model (ug/mL)" = conc_model,
    "Figure 2 mean (ug/mL)" = conc_obs,
    "Model / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Organ tissue concentration at 96 and 168 h, model vs. Figure 2.")
```

With the derived masses, the liver comes out about right, the spleen several
fold too high, and the L2-L4 vertebrae more than an order of magnitude too
high. The vertebral result means that, read as amounts, the printed constants
put about 10% of the dose into three vertebrae.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the simulated blood concentrations, one subject per
fraction. Table 3 gives blood Cmax, half-life, MRT, clearance and total AUC.
The AUC is printed in ug.min/mL and is converted to ug.h/mL (divided by 60)
for the comparison, and the clearance in mL/min is converted to mL/h.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, fraction) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, fraction, time, .keep_all = TRUE)

dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, fraction) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_ug)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | fraction + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | fraction + id, route = "intravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE,
  mrt.obs = TRUE,
  cl.obs = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fraction, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,     ~half.life, ~mrt.obs, ~cl.obs,
  "F1",      0.308, 1708.1 / 60,     83.6,       114.1,    1.03 * 60,
  "F2",      0.326, 1983.7 / 60,     83.8,       116.0,    0.74 * 60
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "fraction",
  units = c(
    cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "h",
    mrt.obs = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published (Table 3 means) blood NCA. * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

Only clearance matches, and it matches by construction, because the model
takes clearance directly from Table 3. Cmax is the concentration right after
the bolus, Dose / Vd, which is about 20-25% below the printed mean. AUC,
half-life and MRT are all off by a large factor. The next section explains
why no amount-based reading of the printed constants can match them.

## Structural checks

These checks compare the solve with closed-form results computed from the
same parameters, so they test the implementation rather than the paper.
With elimination from blood only, AUC from zero to infinity must equal
Dose / CL. For the Figure 3 topology, the steady-state volume is
`Vss = V1 * (1 + k12/k21 + k14/k43 + (k13 + k14)/k31 + k15/k51)` (the `k15`
term is zero here), and the blood MRT must equal `Vss / CL`.

```{r structural-checks}
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "mrt.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(fraction, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

closed_form <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(models), function(fr) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(models[[fr]]))$theta
  k <- exp(p[c(
    "lkin_bonemarrow", "lkout_bonemarrow", "lkin_liver", "lkout_liver",
    "lkin_spleen", "lk_spleen_liver"
  )])
  cl <- exp(p[["lcl"]])
  vc <- exp(p[["lvc"]])
  vss_ratio <- 1 + k[["lkin_bonemarrow"]] / k[["lkout_bonemarrow"]] +
    k[["lkin_spleen"]] / k[["lk_spleen_liver"]] +
    (k[["lkin_liver"]] + k[["lkin_spleen"]]) / k[["lkout_liver"]]
  tibble::tibble(
    fraction = fr,
    auc_closed = dose_ug / cl,
    mrt_closed = vss_ratio * vc / cl,
    vss_ratio = vss_ratio
  )
}))

checks <- dplyr::inner_join(nca_wide, closed_form, by = "fraction")
stopifnot(
  nrow(checks) == 2L,
  # Same parameters on both sides: the only difference is trapezoidal and
  # extrapolation error on a fine grid, measured at < 0.5%.
  all(abs(checks$aucinf.obs / checks$auc_closed - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(checks$mrt.obs / checks$mrt_closed - 1) < 0.01)
)

checks |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Fraction" = fraction,
    "AUCinf, PKNCA (ug*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "Dose / CL (ug*h/mL)" = auc_closed,
    "MRT, PKNCA (h)" = mrt.obs,
    "Vss / CL (h)" = mrt_closed,
    "Vss / V1" = vss_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated blood AUC and MRT vs. their closed forms.")
```

# Internal consistency of the published parameters

Table 3 reports the arithmetic means of per-patient estimates, and a model
built from mean parameters need not reproduce the mean of per-patient
summary statistics. The gaps here are too large for that to be the whole
explanation, though, and several are structural:

* **MRT and half-life.** With elimination only from blood, the MRT of an
  amount model is `Vss / CL`. The printed `k12/k21`, `k14/k43` and
  `(k13 + k14)/k31` alone already give `Vss / V1` of about 5.4 (F1) and 4.2
  (F2), so the blood MRT is at least about 360-380 h. Table 3 prints
  114.1 h and 116.0 h. Any positive `k15` / `k51` would only lengthen it.
  The same holds for the terminal half-life, which comes out about four
  times the printed 83.6 / 83.8 h.
* **AUC and clearance.** For a 1 mg dose, Dose / AUC from the printed mean
  AUC is 0.59 mL/min (F1) and 0.50 mL/min (F2), against printed clearances
  of 1.03 and 0.74 mL/min. (The F1 clearance has a large spread, SD 0.73.)
* **Cmax and volume.** Dose / Vd is 0.242 ug/mL (F1) against a printed blood
  Cmax of 0.308 ug/mL.
* **Organ amounts.** Read as amounts, the printed vertebral exchange
  constants put about 100 ug (10% of the dose) into the L2-L4 vertebrae by
  96 h, which is an order of magnitude more than Figure 2 shows.

Kinetica can parameterise exchange on amounts or on concentrations, and the
paper does not say which was used. A reading in which the organ
compartments are concentration "satellites" driven by blood, without
draining it, reproduces the organ curves better. That reading contradicts
the mass-flow arrows of Figure 3, though, and it still needs values for
`k15` / `k51`, which the paper does not report. The maintainers therefore
packaged Figure 3 as drawn, with the printed values only.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Deep compartment.** Figure 3 draws a deep compartment (remaining organs
  and tumor) exchanging with blood through `k15` / `k51`, but no value is
  printed in the text, Table 3 or the Discussion, and the article has no
  supplement. Both are fixed to 0 (`kin_other`, `kout_other`), so the
  `other` state stays empty. A user who has values can set them in `ini()`.
- **State basis.** The rate constants are taken to act on amounts, so the
  model conserves mass along every arrow of Figure 3. The paper does not
  state the basis.
- **Spleen row labels.** Table 3 labels the spleen rate constants 'k13' and
  'k31', the same as the liver row. Figure 3 gives the spleen exactly two
  arrows, uptake from blood (`k14`) and drainage to the liver (`k43`), so
  the first spleen value is read as `k14` and the second as `k43`.
- **Typical values.** The individual Kinetica fits were summarised as mean
  (SD) (Table 3), and no population model was fitted. The packaged models
  use the means and carry no between-subject variability. For reference,
  the F1 SDs are: Vd 937.1 mL, CL 0.73 mL/min, k12 1.31E-4, k21 0.55E-4,
  k13 (liver) 0.60E-4, k31 (liver) 1.07E-4, k14 (spleen) 1.39E-4 and
  k43 (spleen) 0.50E-4 min^-1. No residual error model is reported, and
  none is included.
- **Dose.** The model is in ug of antibody. The 111In imaging dose of
  138 MBq at 138 MBq/mg corresponds to 1 mg. Radioactive decay is not part
  of the model: the paper decay-corrected all measurements (Methods,
  'Determination of amounts of radiolabeled mAbs in blood').
- **Infusion duration.** This is not reported, and the dose is simulated as
  a bolus into blood.
- **Volume of distribution in the Discussion.** The Discussion quotes the F2
  Vd as 4064.3 mL, while Table 3 prints 4064.8 mL. The table value is used.
- **Organ masses.** The organ masses used to turn simulated tissue amounts
  into Figure 2 concentrations are derived from Table 2 (a ratio of means)
  and are not paper values. They are used only in this article's plots,
  not in the model.
- **Figure 2 values** were read from the published figure by the
  maintainers, for comparison only.
- **Errata.** EuropePMC lists no correction notice for the article (checked
  2026-11-25).
